title: White Huns
capsule: The White Huns (Hephthalites) were a Central Asian nomadic confederation that emerged in Bactria c. 410 AD, conquered the Kushano-Sasanian buffer zone, and by the mid-5th century had overrun the Gupta Empire's northwestern provinces, killing the Gupta emperor Skandagupta's successors and reducing much of northwestern India to tributary status. At their apex c. 480–520 their domain extended from the Aral Sea through Afghanistan and into the Punjab, and their king Mihirakula (r. c. 515–540) conducted brutal campaigns in Kashmir and the Gangetic plain. They were destroyed as a coherent polity by a combined Sasanian-Göktürk offensive c. 557–565, dividing their territory between the two powers.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Hephthalite territorial extent is reconstructed from Chinese (Wei Shu, Bei Shi), Byzantine (Procopius), and Armenian sources, supplemented by numismatic evidence; boundaries are broadly estimated and the southern Indian frontier in particular is debated among scholars.
